title: Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry Insights into the Assembly of Lanthanide-Containing Clusters
claim: Preselected organic ligands can direct lanthanide-cluster formation by limiting the coordination sites available for water binding and hydrolysis.
explanation: Ligand-controlled hydrolysis permits the resulting hydroxo species to bridge lanthanide ions while the ligands protect the growing cluster. The review cites amino-acid-, inositol-, and carboxylate-protected cluster families.
scope: Lanthanide oxo/hydroxo clusters formed through hydrolysis in the presence of coordinating organic ligands.
conditions: Ligands occupy part of the lanthanide coordination sphere before or during hydrolysis.
caveats: Large and variable lanthanide coordination spheres make structural control difficult; a particular product may depend on several strategies acting together.
